items.note: The prompt only says 'large order tables'. It never gives the roughly 2 million row figure or says memory use matters. Streaming the writes is asked for, but only as a speed fix.
It says not to change the signature or touch other callers. The 'three callers' detail is left out.
It lists the header line and column order under behaviour to preserve.
It says 'Don't add files' but never forbids new dependencies.
It names the one-query-per-order N+1 pattern as the likely cause and asks for a JOIN or one batched lookup.
It asks for rows to be written to the file as they are produced instead of concatenating a string.
It tells the receiver to list CSV escaping of names with commas as a problem but not fix it, and to keep the output byte-for-byte the same. The person wants proper quoting.
It says to find the existing tests and run them, but doesn't name tests/test_export.py. It also allows a fallback for when there are no tests, though the tests do exist.
It asks for small, surgical edits, not a rewrite, and limits the scope to the one function.

invented: The query text `SELECT name FROM customers`, run once per order
The output is built with `out += ...` before writing
The output file must stay byte-for-byte the same (a requirement the person never gave)
An order with a missing customer raises AttributeError because `cust` is None
